newsitem.title: USA: GM, UAW continue talks in pickup truck strike.
newsitem.headline: GM, UAW continue talks in pickup truck strike.

text.p: General Motors Corp. and its union workers Monday reported some progress in a nine-week-old strike at a GM pickup truck plant following three days of intense negotiations.

Bargainers for GM and United Auto Workers Local 594 resumed discussions at the Pontiac East plant Monday morning, said GM spokesman Dan Flores. Negotiators had started talking at 9 a.m. Friday and took a break at 12:30 a.m. Monday, he said.
"Obviously we're pleased that the negotiations are picking up and intensifying," said Flores, who declined to characterise the discussions.
Terry Underwood, a spokesman for the UAW, said the talks are showing signs of progress.
"There's a little bit of movement occurring," he said. "They are negotiating a little bit stronger than they have in the past."

About 5,800 union workers walked off the job April 22 when talks over a new contract collapsed. The union is demanding GM add several hundred more jobs to ease overtime strains and live up to previous promises.
GM officials have said they are trying to keep staffing down to compete with other automakers and because a new generation pickup trucks requires fewer workers to assemble.
The Pontiac facility is one of three GM plants that make its full-size pickup trucks, and one of two that produce the popular extended cab versions.
CSM Forecasting Inc. Managing Director Michael Robinet estimated GM had lost 58,752 units as of June 19.
GM stock fell 37.5 cents to $55.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
